paper.title: Efficient Learning in Large-Scale Combinatorial Semi-Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial semi-bandit with linear generalization, coherent Gaussian case (Bayesian)
unmapped: Each of L ground items has a known feature vector phi_e in R^d (||phi_e||_2<=1); mean item weights are linear in features: w_bar = Phi theta*
Feasible sets are arbitrary subsets of at most m (paper's K) items out of L items
Learner knows the feature (generalization) matrix Phi and uses an offline combinatorial oracle
Prior on theta* is N(0, lambda^2 I) and the learner knows lambda
settings.definition_quote: If (1) $\bar{\bw}=\Phi \theta^\ast$, (2) the prior on $\theta^\ast$ is $N(0, \lambda^2 I)$, and (3) $\forall (t,e)$, the noise $\eta_t(e)=\bw_t(e)-\bar{\bw}(e)$ is independently sampled from $N(0 , \sigma^2)$ ... We henceforth refer to a case satisfying condition (1)-(3) as a coherent Gaussian case.

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial semi-bandit with linear generalization, coherent learning case, bounded independent weights
unmapped: Each of L ground items has a known feature vector phi_e in R^d (||phi_e||_2<=1); mean item weights are linear in features: w_bar = Phi theta*
Item weights are statistically independent across items under P
Feasible sets are arbitrary subsets of at most m (paper's K) items
Learner knows the feature matrix Phi and uses an offline combinatorial oracle
settings.definition_quote: Under the assumptions that (1) the support of $P$ is a subset of $[0,1]^L$, (2) the stochastic item weights $\left \{ \bw(e) \right \}_{e \in E}$ are statistically independent under $P$, and (3) the oracle $\oracle$ \emph{exactly} solves the offline optimization problem, we have the following upper bound on $R(n)$ when $\comblinucb$ is applied to coherent learning cases

symbols.lambda_p: prior standard deviation lambda of theta* ~ N(0, lambda^2 I), also the algorithm parameter

conditions: prior on theta* is N(0, lambda^2 I)
tuning: CombLinTS run with parameters (Phi, lambda, sigma) matching the prior and noise

source.label: thm:bound_combts
source.quote: If (1) $\bar{\bw}=\Phi \theta^\ast$, (2) the prior on $\theta^\ast$ is $N(0, \lambda^2 I)$, (3) the noises are i.i.d. sampled from $N(0 , \sigma^2)$, and (4) $\lambda \geq \sigma$, then under $\comblints$ algorithm with parameter $(\Phi, \lambda, \sigma)$, we have R_{\mathrm{Bayes}}(n) \leq \tilde{O} \left( K \lambda \sqrt{dn \min \left\{\ln(L), d \right\}} \right).

results.notes: Paper's K (max set size) mapped to m, n to T. Regret is against the oracle solution A* for the mean weights. Compute is efficient given an efficient offline oracle.

symbols.lambda_p: prior standard deviation lambda of theta* ~ N(0, lambda^2 I), also the algorithm parameter

conditions: prior on theta* is N(0, lambda^2 I)
tuning: CombLinTS run with parameters (Phi, lambda, sigma) matching the prior and noise

source.label: thm:bound_1_refine
source.quote: If (1) $\bar{\bw}=\Phi \theta^\ast$, (2) the prior on $\theta^\ast$ is $N(0, \lambda^2 I)$, and (3) the noises are i.i.d. sampled from $N(0 , \sigma^2)$, then under $\combts$ algorithm with parameter $(\Phi, \lambda, \sigma)$, then we have R_{\mathrm{Bayes}}(n) \leq 1+K \lambda \min \{ \sqrt{\ln (\frac{\lambda L n}{\sqrt{2 \pi}} )}, \sqrt{d \ln ( \frac{2d Kn \lambda}{\sqrt{2 \pi}})} \} \sqrt{\frac{2d n \ln ( 1 + \frac{nK \lambda^2}{d} )}{\ln(1+ \frac{\lambda^2}{\sigma^2} )}}.

results.notes: Expression as printed (the inner log term omits sigma^2 in the denominator, as printed; proof's Lemma 4 has nK lambda^2/(d sigma^2)). Paper's K -> m, n -> T. The proof's lemmas actually require a factor sqrt(2) in c, but the theorem is recorded as stated.

symbols.sigma_a: algorithm parameter sigma of CombLinUCB (controls covariance decrease rate)

conditions: support of P is a subset of [0,1]^L
item weights statistically independent under P
oracle exactly solves the offline problem
tuning: c >= (1/sigma) sqrt(d ln(1 + nK lambda^2/(d sigma^2)) + 2 ln(1/delta)) + ||theta*||_2/lambda

source.label: thm:bound_comblinucb
source.quote: For any $\lambda, \sigma>0$, any $\delta \in (0,1)$, and any $c$ satisfying c \geq \frac{1}{\sigma} \sqrt{d \ln ( 1+ \frac{n K \lambda^2}{d \sigma^2}) + 2 \ln ( \frac{1}{\delta} )} + \frac{\| \theta^* \|_2}{\lambda}, if $\bar{\bw} = \Phi \theta^\ast$ and the above three assumptions hold, then under $\comblinucb$ algorithm with parameter $(\Phi, \lambda, \sigma, c)$, we have R(n) \leq 2c  K \lambda\sqrt{...} + nK \delta.

results.notes: R(n) is expected regret vs A* with fixed mean weights, equal to pseudo-regret. Paper notes that with lambda=sigma=1, delta=1/(nK) and minimal c the bound is O_tilde(K d sqrt(n)) (i.e. m d sqrt(T)). c depends on n and ||theta*||, so T and S are known.

symbols.gamma_o: sub-optimality gap of the approximation oracle: f(A*(w),w) >= (1-gamma) max_A f(A,w)

conditions: support of P is a subset of [0,1]^L
item weights statistically independent under P
oracle has sub-optimality gap gamma in [0,1)
tuning: c >= (1/sigma) sqrt(d ln(1 + nK lambda^2/(d sigma^2)) + 2 ln(1/delta)) + ||theta*||_2/lambda

source.label: thm:bound_comblinucb_variant
